evidence: io.lisp:3938-3943: `(stage (fnn-join dir (format nil ".node-secret-~d-~a.stage" ...))) (fd (fnn-open stage (logior sb-posix:o-wronly sb-posix:o-creat sb-posix:o-excl) #o600))) (unwind-protect (progn (fnn-write-all fd octets) (fnn-fsync-file fd)) (fnn-close fd))`. Only the later rename failure unlinks the stage (io.lisp:3946).
fix: Unlink the stage on any failure before the rename (unwind-protect with a done flag, as fnn-write-staged-at :unlink-on-failure does). Or stage under staging/ like create, so the existing sweep owns it.

reviewer: fnn-node-secret-rotate (io.lisp:3938-3943) creates .node-secret-PID-HEX.stage in the keys directory. If fnn-write-all or fnn-fsync-file fails, the unwind-protect only closes the fd, and the unlink at io.lisp:3946 runs only when the replace fails. fnn-sweep-staging (io.lisp:2291) enumerates staging/, not keys/, so a partial file of new secret material (mode 0600) stays behind. It needs ENOSPC or EIO during an operator rotate.
scenario: During `store ROOT node-secret rotate`, the write fails (ENOSPC or EIO) or the fsync fails. The fd is closed but the half-written stage, which holds part of the new epoch's root secret, stays in STORE/keys/. The staging sweep only enumerates STORE/staging, so nothing ever collects it. Repeated failures pile up files of secret material under random names, and they would leave the node in any backup of keys/. node-secret create stages under staging/ and is swept; rotate is not.
title: A failed node-secret rotation leaves a partial secret file in keys/, which no sweep removes
